```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
library(knitr)
suppressMessages(devtools::load_all("../../RESI", quiet = TRUE))
source("../../tests/star_data.R")

school <- "sch"; child_grp <- "sid:sch"
star <- load_star()
truth_fit <- lme4::lmer(form_star, data = star, REML = FALSE,
                        control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
lyu <- lyuLimitResi(truth_fit, school, child_grp)
full_resi <- suppressMessages(resi(truth_fit, vcovfunc = stats::vcov, level = 2, ci.method = "qf"))

cal <- readRDS("star_plasmode_summary.rds")
cal_resi <- readRDS("star_plasmode_resi_summary.rds")
ci_cov <- readRDS("star_ci_coverage.rds")
ci_cov <- ci_cov[ci_cov$engine == "lmer", ]

expected_m <- lapply(setNames(nm = sort(unique(cal_resi$n_per_site))),
                     function(m) expectedDesignResi(truth_fit, m, school, child_grp))
cal_resi$expected_resi_m <- mapply(function(tab, term, m) {
  expected_m[[as.character(m)]][[tab]][term, "RESI"]
}, cal_resi$table, cal_resi$term, cal_resi$n_per_site)

# Terms, their level and colours are all derived from the fit.
X <- lme4::getME(truth_fit, "X")
coef_terms <- colnames(X)
term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(lme4::nobars(form_star)), "term.labels")
pal <- c("#1F77B4", "#D62728", "#2CA02C", "#FF7F0E", "#9467BD", "#8C564B",
         "#E377C2", "#17BECF", "#BCBD22", "#7F7F7F", "#AEC7E8", "#FFBB78", "#98DF8A")
term_cols <- setNames(rep(pal, length.out = length(coef_terms)), coef_terms)
anova_cols <- setNames(term_cols[match(seq_along(term_labels), attr(X, "assign"))], term_labels)
between_coef <- names(lyu$between)[lyu$between]
between_terms <- c(between_coef, term_labels[vapply(seq_along(term_labels), function(t) {
  all(lyu$between[attr(X, "assign") == t])
}, logical(1L))], paste0("var_", school, "_(Intercept)"))
vc_names <- unique(cal$param[!grepl("^beta_", cal$param)])
vc_cols <- setNames(c("#636363", "#E6550D", "#31A354")[seq_along(vc_names)], vc_names)
```

# Purpose

The mixed-model RESI point estimator, its Lyu–Welsh targets and the
confidence intervals of `notes/resi_mixed_ci.qmd` were developed and
checked on `mlmRev::egsingle`. This report repeats the same hybrid plasmode
on a dataset they were **not** developed on, to check that nothing in the
methods or the simulation framework is tuned to egsingle. The code is
shared: `hybridPlasmodeSim()`, `lyuLimitResi()`, `expectedDesignResi()`,
`designAveragedSe()` and `resi()` in the package, and
`tests/mixed_ci_coverage_lib.R` for the coverage summaries. Only the data
preparation (`tests/star_data.R`) and the driver
(`tests/run_star_validation.R`) are new.

# Dataset and model

`mlmRev::star` is the Tennessee STAR class-size experiment: yearly
mathematics scores (kindergarten to grade 3) for students nested in
schools, the same occasion < student < school nesting as egsingle but with
far fewer occasions per student and different kinds of covariates.

```{r data-size}
n_child <- table(star$sch[!duplicated(star$sid)])
kable(data.frame(
  Quantity = c("schools", "students", "measurements",
               "students per school (min / median / max)", "measurements per student (mean)"),
  Value = c(nlevels(star$sch), nlevels(star$sid), nrow(star),
            paste(range(n_child)[1], median(n_child), range(n_child)[2], sep = " / "),
            round(nrow(star) / nlevels(star$sid), 2))),
  caption = "Complete cases on the model variables")
```

Model (fitted by ML to the full data; the fit is the data-generating truth):

`r paste(deparse(form_star), collapse = " ")`

- `yrs`: years in the study (0–3), varies within student.
- `cltype`: class type (small / regular / regular with aide; reference
  regular), assigned by the experiment and varying within student; a
  2-df within-school term.
- `ses`: free-lunch status (reference not free lunch), varies within student.
- `sx`, `black`: student-level.
- `schtype3`: school type (city = inner-city + urban, suburb, rural); a
  2-df **between-school** factor, which egsingle does not have.
- `fl_10`: school percentage of free-lunch measurements in units of 10
  points; a continuous between-school term.

Rare categories were merged so that resampled designs rarely lose a factor
level (only 7 of 80 schools are urban; about 65 students are neither white
nor black). Replicates that still lose a level are counted as failed fits;
the student id is made unique within school because 446 students appear in
more than one school.

```{r truth}
vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(truth_fit))
kable(data.frame(component = c(vc$grp), variance = vc$vcov,
                 proportion = vc$vcov / sum(vc$vcov)), digits = 3,
      caption = "Variance components of the full-data ML fit")
coef_tab <- full_resi$coefficients
kable(data.frame(term = rownames(coef_tab), level = coef_tab$`n level`,
                 S_Lyu = lyu$coefficients[rownames(coef_tab), "RESI"],
                 S_m25 = expected_m[["25"]]$coefficients[rownames(coef_tab), "RESI"],
                 S_m200 = expected_m[["200"]]$coefficients[rownames(coef_tab), "RESI"],
                 full_data = coef_tab$RESI,
                 coef_tab[, grep("^Var prop", names(coef_tab))], check.names = FALSE),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Coefficient RESI targets: Lyu-Welsh limit, fixed-m expected-design value at m = 25 and 200, and the full-data estimate, with the variance proportions of each covariate")
an_tab <- as.data.frame(full_resi$anova)
kable(data.frame(term = rownames(an_tab), df = an_tab$Df, level = an_tab$`n level`,
                 S_Lyu = lyu$anova[rownames(an_tab), "RESI"],
                 S_m25 = expected_m[["25"]]$anova[rownames(an_tab), "RESI"],
                 S_m200 = expected_m[["200"]]$anova[rownames(an_tab), "RESI"],
                 full_data = an_tab$RESI), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "ANOVA-term RESI targets")
```

Apart from `yrs`, every effect is small, and the between-school effects
(`schtype3`, `fl_10`) are near zero. This tests the intervals in the
near-null regime, which is rarer in egsingle.

# Point-estimate calibration

`hybridPlasmodeSim()` with `n_schools` $\in \{15, 30, 60, 100\}$ ×
`n_per_site` $\in \{25, 100, 200\}$, 1000 replicates per cell (seed 2026).
The figure has the same layout as the egsingle report.

```{r fails}
fits <- unique(cal[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "n_success")])
kable(reshape(fits, idvar = "n_schools", timevar = "n_per_site", direction = "wide"),
      row.names = FALSE, caption = "Successful replicates (of 1000) per cell")
```

```{r fig-cal, fig.width=15, fig.height=18, fig.cap="Hybrid plasmode calibration on STAR, same layout as the egsingle report. Left: between-school terms; middle: terms that vary within school. x-axis: planned students n_schools x n_per_site (log scale); solid lines vary n_per_site at fixed n_schools, dotted lines vary n_schools at fixed n_per_site; point shape marks n_schools. Rows: model SE / MC SD of the fixed effects; variance-component relative bias; scaled MC error SD / Lyu limiting per-unit SE (ticks: design-averaged per-unit SE at that cell); coefficient and ANOVA RESI centred on the Lyu limit (points: simulation means; bands: fixed-m truth S_m). Coefficients are multiplied by sign(S_Lyu)."}
n_per_site.vec <- sort(unique(cal$n_per_site))
n_schools.vec <- sort(unique(cal$n_schools))
school_pch <- setNames(c(15, 16, 17, 18, 8, 4)[seq_along(n_schools.vec)], n_schools.vec)
row_limits <- function(values, reference = 0) {
  limits <- range(c(values, reference), na.rm = TRUE)
  padding <- if (diff(limits) > 0) diff(limits) * 0.08 else 0.05
  limits + c(-padding, padding)
}
plot_combined <- function(df, value_col, ylab, main, ref, cols, ref_col = "gray40",
                          ref_lty = 2, truth_m_col = NULL, per_cell = FALSE) {
  df$N_planned <- df$n_schools * df$n_per_site
  par(mar = c(3.6, 4.0, 2.2, 0.5), mgp = c(2.2, 0.6, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(df$N_planned),
       ylim = row_limits(c(df[[value_col]], if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) df[[truth_m_col]]), ref),
       log = "x", xlab = "planned students (n_schools x n_per_site)", ylab = ylab,
       main = main, bty = "l")
  abline(h = ref, lty = ref_lty, col = ref_col, lwd = 1.5)
  for (term in unique(df$term)) {
    td <- df[df$term == term, ]
    if (!is.null(truth_m_col) && per_cell) {
      segments(td$N_planned * 0.9, td[[truth_m_col]], td$N_planned / 0.9, td[[truth_m_col]],
               col = adjustcolor(cols[[term]], 0.35), lwd = 7, lend = 1)
    } else if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) {
      for (m in n_per_site.vec) {
        s <- td[td$n_per_site == m, ]
        segments(min(s$N_planned), s[[truth_m_col]][1], max(s$N_planned), s[[truth_m_col]][1],
                 col = adjustcolor(cols[[term]], 0.35), lwd = 7, lend = 1)
      }
    }
    for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
      s <- td[td$n_schools == ns, ]; s <- s[order(s$n_per_site), ]
      lines(s$N_planned, s[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]], lwd = 2)
    }
    for (m in n_per_site.vec) {
      s <- td[td$n_per_site == m, ]; s <- s[order(s$n_schools), ]
      lines(s$N_planned, s[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]], lwd = 1.5, lty = 3)
    }
    points(td$N_planned, td[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]],
           pch = school_pch[as.character(td$n_schools)], cex = 1.1)
  }
}
legend_panel <- function(cols, title, band_labels = NULL, ref_col = "gray40", ref_lty = 2) {
  par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
  plot.new()
  legend("top", legend = names(cols), col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85, title = title)
  key <- c(paste("n_schools =", n_schools.vec), "vary n_per_site", "vary n_schools")
  pch <- c(school_pch, NA, NA); lty <- c(rep(NA, length(n_schools.vec)), 1, 3)
  lwd <- c(rep(NA, length(n_schools.vec)), 2, 1.5); col <- rep("black", length(key))
  if (!is.null(band_labels)) {
    key <- c(key, band_labels); pch <- c(pch, NA, NA); lty <- c(lty, ref_lty, 1)
    lwd <- c(lwd, 1.5, 7); col <- c(col, ref_col, adjustcolor("black", 0.35))
  }
  legend("bottom", legend = key, pch = pch, lty = lty, lwd = lwd, col = col, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}
two_cols <- function(df, cols, value_col, ylab, main, ref, legend_title, ref_col = "gray40",
                     ref_lty = 2, truth_m_col = NULL, per_cell = FALSE,
                     band_labels = c("large-m truth (Lyu limit)", "fixed-m truth (S_m)")) {
  is_b <- df$term %in% between_terms
  plot_combined(df[is_b, ], value_col, ylab, paste0("Between-school: ", main), ref, cols,
                ref_col, ref_lty, truth_m_col, per_cell)
  plot_combined(df[!is_b, ], value_col, ylab, paste0("Within-school: ", main), ref, cols,
                ref_col, ref_lty, truth_m_col, per_cell)
  legend_panel(cols[unique(df$term)], legend_title,
               band_labels = if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) band_labels,
               ref_col = ref_col, ref_lty = ref_lty)
}

fe_df <- cal[grepl("^beta_", cal$param), ]
fe_df$term <- sub("^beta_", "", fe_df$param)
design_avg_file <- "star_design_averaged_se.rds"
if (file.exists(design_avg_file)) {
  design_avg_se <- readRDS(design_avg_file)
} else {
  set.seed(20261116)
  cells <- unique(fe_df[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site")])
  design_avg_se <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    se <- designAveragedSe(truth_fit, cells$n_schools[i], cells$n_per_site[i],
                           school = school, child = child_grp)
    data.frame(n_schools = cells$n_schools[i], n_per_site = cells$n_per_site[i],
               term = names(se), se_unit_design_avg = unname(se))
  }))
  saveRDS(design_avg_se, design_avg_file)
}
fe_df <- merge(fe_df, design_avg_se, by = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
fe_df$se_ratio_design_avg <- fe_df$se_unit_design_avg / fe_df$truth_se_scaled
vc_df <- cal[!grepl("^beta_", cal$param), ]
vc_df$term <- vc_df$param
vc_df$rel_bias_pct <- 100 * vc_df$bias / vc_df$truth
sgn <- ifelse(cal_resi$truth_resi < 0, -1, 1)
cal_resi$mean_dev <- sgn * (cal_resi$mc_mean_resi - cal_resi$truth_resi)
cal_resi$truth_dev <- sgn * (cal_resi$expected_resi_m - cal_resi$truth_resi)

layout(matrix(1:15, nrow = 5L, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(4.0, 4.0, 1.7))
two_cols(fe_df, term_cols, "se_ratio", "mean_model_se / mc_sd",
         "fixed-effect SE calibration", ref = 1, legend_title = "Fixed effect")
two_cols(vc_df, vc_cols, "rel_bias_pct", "Relative bias (%)",
         "variance-component bias", ref = 0, legend_title = "Variance component")
two_cols(fe_df, term_cols, "scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio", "scaled MC error SD / limiting SE",
         "scaled MC error SD ratio", ref = 1, ref_col = "black", ref_lty = 1,
         legend_title = "Fixed effect", truth_m_col = "se_ratio_design_avg", per_cell = TRUE,
         band_labels = c("large-m limiting SE", "design-averaged SE (g, m)"))
two_cols(cal_resi[cal_resi$table == "coefficients", ], term_cols, "mean_dev",
         "sign(S) x (value - Lyu limit)", "RESI coefficient", ref = 0,
         legend_title = "Coefficient", truth_m_col = "truth_dev")
two_cols(cal_resi[cal_resi$table == "anova", ], anova_cols, "mean_dev", "value - Lyu limit",
         "RESI ANOVA term", ref = 0, legend_title = "ANOVA term", truth_m_col = "truth_dev")
```

```{r cal-tables}
fe_tab <- fe_df[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term", "se_ratio",
                    "scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio", "se_ratio_design_avg")]
kable(fe_tab[order(fe_tab$term, fe_tab$n_schools, fe_tab$n_per_site), ], digits = 3,
      row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Fixed effects: model SE / MC SD, and scaled MC error SD and design-averaged SE relative to the Lyu limiting per-unit SE")
rt <- cal_resi[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term", "truth_resi",
                   "expected_resi_m", "mc_mean_resi", "mc_sd_resi")]
names(rt)[5:6] <- c("S_Lyu", "S_m")
kable(rt[order(rt$table, rt$term, rt$n_schools, rt$n_per_site), ], digits = 3,
      row.names = FALSE, caption = "RESI: targets and simulation mean and SD")
```

# Confidence interval coverage

As for egsingle: `n_schools` $\in \{15, 100\}$ × `n_per_site`
$\in \{25, 200\}$, 1000 replicates per cell (seed 2027), intervals from
`resi()`'s internal `.resi_ci_mixed()` with the model-based and CR2
(school-clustered) covariances and the normal, QF and CF methods, scored
against $S_m$ and $S_{\text{Lyu}}$. Grey band: $0.95 \pm 1.96$ Monte Carlo
SE. Solid lines are between-school terms.

```{r ci-coverage, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 12}
cells <- c("g15m25", "g15m200", "g100m25", "g100m200")
ci_cov$cell <- factor(paste0("g", ci_cov$n_schools, "m", ci_cov$n_per_site), cells)
cov_panel <- function(d, target, main, cols) {
  y <- d[[paste0("coverage_", target)]]
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0.8, 4.2), ylim = c(min(0.5, y, na.rm = TRUE), 1), xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
       ylab = paste("Coverage of", target), main = main)
  axis(1, at = 1:4, labels = c("g=15, m=25", "g=15, m=200", "g=100, m=25", "g=100, m=200"),
       cex.axis = 0.8)
  se <- 1.96 * sqrt(0.95 * 0.05 / 1000)
  rect(0, 0.95 - se, 5, 0.95 + se, col = "gray90", border = NA)
  abline(h = 0.95, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (tm in names(cols)) {
    x <- d[d$term == tm, ]
    x <- x[order(x$cell), ]
    if (!nrow(x)) next
    lines(as.integer(x$cell), x[[paste0("coverage_", target)]], col = cols[[tm]],
          lty = if (x$level[1] == "between") 1 else 2, type = "b", pch = 19)
  }
}
layout(matrix(1:12, nrow = 4L, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(4, 4, 1.7))
for (spec in list(list("coefficients", "normal", term_cols, "coefficient, normal"),
                  list("anova", "qf", anova_cols, "ANOVA, QF"))) {
  for (target in c("S_m", "S_Lyu")) {
    for (cv in c("model", "CR2")) {
      d <- ci_cov[ci_cov$table == spec[[1]] & ci_cov$method == spec[[2]] & ci_cov$covariance == cv, ]
      cov_panel(d, target, paste0(cv, " covariance: ", spec[[4]]), spec[[3]])
    }
    plot.new()
    legend("center", legend = names(spec[[3]]), col = spec[[3]],
           lty = ifelse(names(spec[[3]]) %in% between_terms, 1, 2),
           pch = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.7, y.intersp = 0.85, title = "solid: between school")
  }
}
```

```{r ci-tables}
ci_wide <- reshape(ci_cov[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term", "covariance", "method",
                              "coverage_S_m", "coverage_S_Lyu")],
                   idvar = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term", "covariance"),
                   timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
kable(ci_wide[order(ci_wide$table, ci_wide$covariance, ci_wide$term, ci_wide$n_schools,
                    ci_wide$n_per_site), ], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Coverage of S_m and S_Lyu by method (nominal 0.95; Monte Carlo SE 0.007)")
se_tab <- ci_cov[ci_cov$method == "normal" & ci_cov$table == "coefficients",
                 c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term", "covariance", "mean_se", "mc_sd_est")]
se_tab$ratio <- se_tab$mean_se / se_tab$mc_sd_est
kable(reshape(se_tab[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term", "covariance", "ratio")],
              idvar = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term"), timevar = "covariance",
              direction = "wide"),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Mean estimated SD of the coefficient RESI / Monte Carlo SD")
summ <- aggregate(cbind(coverage_S_m, coverage_S_Lyu) ~ covariance + method + table + n_schools + n_per_site,
                  ci_cov, function(x) c(mean = mean(x), min = min(x)))
summ <- do.call(data.frame, summ)
kable(summ[order(summ$table, summ$covariance, summ$method, summ$n_schools, summ$n_per_site), ],
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Mean and minimum coverage over terms")
```

# Interpretation

The methods behave on STAR as they did on egsingle. One regime that egsingle
did not test (a very large between-school RESI with few schools) exposes a
small-`n_schools` limitation of the normal interval.

- **Point-estimate calibration.**
  - Fixed effects: model SE / MC SD is 0.86–1.05. Values below 0.95 occur
    only for between-school terms at `n_schools = 15`.
  - Variance components: relative bias within ±3%.
  - Within-school RESI: on the Lyu limit at every `n_per_site`.
  - Between-school terms: the scaled MC SD exceeds the Lyu limiting SE
    (1.6–1.7 at `n_per_site = 25`, about 1.07 at 200), and the excess
    follows the design-averaged ticks. The RESI means follow the fixed-m
    bands $S_m$.
  - This is the same finite-m estimand gap as for `size_100`/`lowinc_10` in
    egsingle (school-level precision $g/(\tau^2 + \sigma^2_w/m)$).
- **Failed fits.** 2–3% of replicates at `n_schools = 15` lose a
  school-type level and are dropped (`n_success`). None are lost at
  `n_schools >= 60`.
- **CI coverage of $S_m$, model-based covariance.**
  - Coefficients (normal): 0.92–0.97 at `n_schools = 15` and 0.94–0.97 at
    100, except the intercept.
  - ANOVA terms with QF: 0.92–0.99. The normal ANOVA interval undercovers
    the small within-school terms at `n_schools = 15` (`sx` 0.84, `black`
    0.82, `ses` 0.88) and `sx` at `n_schools = 100`, `n_per_site = 25`
    (0.81). QF and CF fix this, as in egsingle.
  - The near-null between-school terms (`schtype3`, `fl_10`, $|S| < 0.07$)
    are conservative (0.95–0.99), as expected for intervals near the
    boundary.
- **The intercept at `n_schools = 15`** covers at only about 0.77–0.79.
  - The STAR intercept RESI is very large ($S_m \approx 8$–10, against
    about 0.2 in egsingle). Its estimator scales like
    $1/\hat\tau_{\text{school}}$, and with 15 schools $\hat\tau$ is very
    uncertain. The sampling distribution is therefore right-skewed, and the
    delta-method SD underestimates the MC SD by about 20%.
  - At `n_schools = 100` the intercept covers $S_m$ at 0.94–0.95. Its
    $S_{\text{Lyu}}$ coverage is low (0.36 at `n_per_site = 25`, 0.90 at
    200), because the fixed-m gap (8.4 vs 10.6) is large relative to the
    interval width.
  - A skewness-aware or $t_{g-1}$-based interval (review question 4 of
    `notes/resi_mixed_ci.qmd`) would be the natural remedy. The current
    defaults were not changed.
- **CI coverage, CR2 covariance.** As in egsingle: 0.86–0.94 for
  coefficients at `n_schools = 15`, where the estimated SD is up to 38% too
  small (few clusters), and 0.92–0.96 at `n_schools = 100`. The intercept
  is about 0.78 and 0.90.
- **$S_{\text{Lyu}}$ coverage** equals the $S_m$ coverage for within-school
  terms and for the near-null between-school terms (whose fixed-m gap is
  tiny relative to the interval width). It drops for the intercept, as
  above.

Nothing in the methods needed to change for this dataset. The only
dataset-specific code is the data preparation in `tests/star_data.R`.
The terms, their levels (between/within) and all targets are derived from
the fitted model by the shared package and library code.
